Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The potions go into the NEW belt slots. AlchemicalCoffer.cs:22 snapshots `originalSlotCount = Owner.MaxPotionCount` BEFORE :23 grows the belt, and :27 procures each potion into the EXPLICIT slot `originalSlotCount + i` -- on a fresh belt slots 3, 4, 5, 6, leaving 0-2 empty. relics/alchemical_coffer.py called `run.add_potion(potion)` per potion, and `RunState.add_potion` fills the FIRST open slot, so the sim filled 0-3. `add_potion` now takes an optional explicit `slot`, which is the other form `PotionCmd.TryToProcure` takes, and the relic passes `original_slots + i`. EXECUTED on a fresh run: max 3 -> 7 with slots 0-2 None and 3-6 filled, where the sim used to leave 4-6 empty. Slot identity is not cosmetic -- a UsePotion replay command names a SLOT and the conformance runner diffs `floor_potions` slot by slot, which is the whole reason this was re-verdicted from waiver under the record's own scope ruling. The counts and the two CombatPotionGeneration draws per potion were already right and are untouched. Pinned by test/test_relic_live_tail.py::test_alchemical_coffer_fills_the_new_slots_only. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: SCOPE RULING (2026-07-26 relic fix pass, applied at every potion site in this tier). The shared contract's 'Out of scope everywhere: potions (deferred by Perry)' means POTION IS NOT AN AUDITED KIND -- there is no `potion` roster kind and no `audit/records/potion/`. It does NOT mean that potion-affecting behaviour of an AUDITED relic is invisible. The relic tier itself already reads it that way at the overwhelming majority of its sites: 45 relic gap entries across 25 records turn on potion mechanics, 27 of them tagged LIVE (relic/belt_buckle, relic/cauldron, relic/sozu, relic/delicate_frond, relic/petrified_toad, relic/tiny_mailbox, relic/white_beast_statue, relic/wongos_mystery_ticket, relic/phial_holster G1 ...), against only four records that waived on the exclusion. Binding rule 3 forces one answer and the majority is also the better-reasoned side: potions ARE ported (51 registered classes, 48 in the reward pool) and the belt is conformance-asserted -- sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:623-631 diffs `floor_potions` slot by slot and sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:715-717 reads `max_potions`. A divergence the conformance runner asserts on is by definition one a replay sees, which is the README's definition of a gap.
AT THIS SITE (LIVE, grade B): the counts and the RNG stream are both right -- 4 slots, 4 potions, and sts2_rl/relics/alchemical_coffer.py:24-28 spends the same two CombatPotionGeneration draws per potion the source does (verified against `PotionFactory.CreateRandomPotion`, src/Core/Factories/PotionFactory.cs:67-81). The divergence is the SLOT INDEX. AlchemicalCoffer.cs:22 snapshots `originalSlotCount = Owner.MaxPotionCount`, line 23 grows the belt, and line 27 procures each potion into the EXPLICIT slot `originalSlotCount + i` -- on a fresh belt, slots 3, 4, 5, 6. sts2_rl/relics/alchemical_coffer.py:31-32 calls `run.add_potion(potion)` per potion, and `RunState.add_potion` fills the FIRST open slot (`self.potions[self.potions.index(None)] = potion`, sts2_rl/run.py:484). EXECUTED on a fresh run: belt before `max=3 [None, None, None]`; after `add_relic('alchemical_coffer')`, `max=7` with slots [0 fairy_in_a_bottle, 1 colorless_potion, 2 liquid_memories, 3 strength_potion, 4 None, 5 None, 6 None] -- the game would leave 0-2 empty and fill 3-6. Slot identity is NOT cosmetic here: `UsePotion` replay commands name a SLOT (see the project's 'Potion belt + profile names' note), and sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:623-631 diffs `floor_potions` slot by slot. Reachable with ported content: Alchemical Coffer is one of the three OPTION_POOL_2 relics of the ported Orobas shrine (sts2_rl/events/orobas.py:21). Re-verdicted from waiver -- see the scope ruling above. Rule 7: src/Core/Factories/PotionFactory.cs, sts2_rl/run.py and sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py are cited and not hashed by this record.
